parts.name: Anterosuperior quadrant
parts.attachment_or_location: anterosuperior glenoid rim, continuous with the long head of biceps origin
parts.function_note: more mobile and loosely attached than the inferior labrum, and the classic site of a SLAP (superior labrum anterior-posterior) tear given its direct continuity with the biceps anchor.
parts.source: Cooper DE, Arnoczky SP, O'Brien SJ, Warren RF, DiCarlo E, Allen AA (1992) 'Anatomy, histology, and vascularity of the glenoid labrum: an anatomical study.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 74(1):46-52 -- glenoid labrum regional structure and vascularity.

parts.name: Posteroinferior quadrant
parts.attachment_or_location: posteroinferior glenoid rim, continuous with the inferior glenohumeral ligament's axillary pouch
parts.function_note: more firmly fibrocartilaginous and immobile than the superior labrum, and mechanically more important to anteroinferior shoulder stability given its continuity with the IGHL complex.
parts.source: Cooper DE, Arnoczky SP, O'Brien SJ, Warren RF, DiCarlo E, Allen AA (1992) 'Anatomy, histology, and vascularity of the glenoid labrum: an anatomical study.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 74(1):46-52 -- glenoid labrum regional structure and vascularity.

function: A fibrocartilaginous rim deepening the shallow glenoid fossa by roughly 50% (per Howell & Galinat 1989), substantially increasing the socket's effective depth and the glenohumeral joint's stability without sacrificing its wide range of motion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Cooper DE, Arnoczky SP, O'Brien SJ, Warren RF, DiCarlo E, Allen AA (1992) 'Anatomy, histology, and vascularity of the glenoid labrum: an anatomical study.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 74(1):46-52 -- glenoid labrum regional structure and vascularity.; Howell SM, Galinat BJ (1989) 'The glenoid-labral socket: a constrained articular surface.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 243:122-125 -- the actual source of the glenoid labrum's approximately 50% depth-increase figure (Cooper et al. 1992, used for the top-level entity's regional-attachment/vascularity claims, does not itself quantify depth increase -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

parts.name: Anterosuperior quadrant
parts.function_note: the thinnest, most vulnerable region and the most common site of labral tears, per Seldes et al.'s (2001) cadaveric series -- though that series specifically studied age-related degenerative tears in elderly specimens (mean age 78) and predates femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) as a defined clinical concept (Ganz et al. 2003); anterosuperior predominance is also separately well-documented in the FAI literature, but that is a distinct body of work from this specific citation (scope corrected after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
parts.source: Seldes RM, Tan V, Hunt J, Katz M, Winiarsky R, Fitzgerald RH Jr (2001) 'Anatomy, histologic features, and vascularity of the adult acetabular labrum.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 382:232-240 -- acetabular labrum regional structure and vascularity.

parts.name: Posteroinferior quadrant
parts.attachment_or_location: posteroinferior acetabular rim, continuous with the transverse acetabular ligament
parts.function_note: thicker and less frequently torn than the anterosuperior region.
parts.source: Seldes RM, Tan V, Hunt J, Katz M, Winiarsky R, Fitzgerald RH Jr (2001) 'Anatomy, histologic features, and vascularity of the adult acetabular labrum.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 382:232-240 -- acetabular labrum regional structure and vascularity.

function: A fibrocartilaginous ring deepening the acetabulum and, together with its attached capsule, creating a suction-seal effect (per Ferguson et al. 2003's fluid-mechanics testing) that contributes to hip joint stability and synovial fluid pressurization/lubrication.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Seldes RM, Tan V, Hunt J, Katz M, Winiarsky R, Fitzgerald RH Jr (2001) 'Anatomy, histologic features, and vascularity of the adult acetabular labrum.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 382:232-240 -- acetabular labrum regional structure and vascularity.; Ferguson SJ, Bryant JT, Ganz R, Ito K (2003) 'An in vitro investigation of the acetabular labral seal in hip joint mechanics.' J Biomech 36(2):171-178 -- the actual source of the labral 'suction seal' fluid-mechanics finding (Seldes et al. 2001, used elsewhere in this entity for the anterosuperior tear-location claim, is a histology/tear-pattern study of elderly cadavers and does not address fluid mechanics or FAI, a clinical concept introduced by Ganz et al. in 2003 -- two years after Seldes' paper -- so the FAI framing has also been removed here; caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
